newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-PRIVATISATION AGENCY KEEPS CURRENT DIRECTORS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-PRIVATISATION AGENCY KEEPS CURRENT DIRECTORS.

text.p: The Latvian privatisation agency (LPA) on Friday said that it has retained two current directors whose jobs were offered in a competition to replace them.
The two board members, Arvis Freibergs, technical manager, and Andrejs Tiknuss, privatisation process manager, were kept although 18 people applied for their jobs.

"The current holders of the positons were the best candidates. They were chosen because of their experience, their knowledge of the privatisation process and because of their personal qualities," said Michael Clark, manager of accountants Deloitte and Touche, which organised the competition.
The competition was organised as a compromise after Economy Minister Guntar Krasts blocked the renewal of the directors' mandates.
LPA chief Janis Naglis was not surprised by the result.
"I did not expect anything else...the main drawback of the other candidates was lack of experience," he said.
The competition results still have to be approved by Krasts.
